detail.abstract: This work presents the first empirical evidence of a fundamental computational phase transition in the architecture of machine intelligence, identifying a previously unreported mathematical regime defined by sub-linear to linear operational scaling, absolute deterministic stability, and extreme energy-bounded execution. For the past decade, the trajectory of artificial intelligence, and specifically large sequence modeling, has been inextricably constrained by the quadratic scaling laws inherent to Transformer architectures. In this prevailing paradigm, the computational and thermodynamic costs of sequence routing grow exponentially with context length, precipitating catastrophic structural and thermal failure at extended horizons. This paper introduces the empirical phenomenology of the Fractal and Pyramid computational substrates, documenting their isolated behavioral envelopes across massive sequence boundaries. The experimental results demonstrate a violent discontinuity in established scaling behavior. As context windows scale from 2,000 to 512,000 tokens, standard Transformer architectures demand an operation count explosion from to operations, culminating in irrecoverable architectural timeouts past the 64k–128k boundary. In stark contrast, the Pyramid substrate processes 512,000 tokens utilizing merely 40,139 operations, exhibiting a terminal scaling exponent of . At the 1,000,000-token threshold, the thermodynamic divergence becomes a definitive phase shift: while a theoretical Transformer expends 3,000 Joules of CPU energy, the Pyramid regime executes the identical sequence length utilizing an infinitesimally small Joules—an efficiency gain exceeding seven orders of magnitude. Furthermore, the Fractal and Pyramid regimes demonstrate absolute zero-drift stability over repeated long-horizon executions, providing empirical proof of a reversible, machine-precision, chaos-bounded primitive. The identification of this sub-linear, energy-bounded, and drift-free mathematical envelope suggests the existence of a new computational substrate that effectively obsoletes the Transformer. This discovery challenges the dominance of quadratic-scaling architectures, shattering the physical and thermodynamic limits of continuous sequence modeling. Beyond the strict mathematical implications, this substrate shift promises to radically alter the structural economics of the global compute market. By nullifying the massive capital requirements imposed by energy-explosive models, the Pyramid regime dismantles the artificial structural barriers centralizing compute power, thereby democratizing the architecture of intelligence and fundamentally disrupting entrenched industry monopolies.

title: Simulation-Based Optimization of Emergency Medical Resource Allocation for Post-Earthquake Surge Conditions: A Nepal Case Study
affiliations: Pokhara University, Pokhara University, Pokhara University, Pokhara University, Pokhara University and Tribhuvan University

detail.title: Simulation-Based Optimization of Emergency Medical Resource Allocation for Post-Earthquake Surge Conditions: A Nepal Case Study
detail.abstract: Emergency medical systems in seismically active developing nations face severe surge conditions that overwhelm static resource allocations within hours of a major event. In Nepal where the 2015 earthquake caused more than 9,000 deaths and displaced approximately two million people, this highlighted infrastructural vulnerability, geographic complexity, and constrained health-system. Yet most operational frameworks for post-earthquake response remain deterministic or paper-based, offering little support for multi-objective resource distribution decisions.This study develops and evaluates a simulation-optimization framework for post-earthquake emergency medical resource allocation, modeled on Nepal's district-level health infrastructure. A discrete-event simulation captures patient flow under stochastic demand, incorporating epicenter-based arrival rates, two-phase temporal decay, and an explicit mortality penalty to prevent optimizer exploitation of patient deprioritization. Six optimization algorithms are compared: Grid Search, Random Search, Simulated Annealing, Bayesian Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and a proposed hybrid combining random exploration with genetic refinement across three objective functions: minimization of global wait time, maximization of patient throughput, and a composite metric.The hybrid algorithm achieves the strongest performance in single-objective scenarios, attaining 91.4\% improvement over baseline on wait-time minimization and 110.2\% improvement over baseline on patient throughput. Under the composite objective, it matches the best genetic solution at 116.9\% improvement over baseline while converging in 50 iterations compared to 360 for the standalone genetic approach. These results demonstrate that hybrid metaheuristic methods offer a computationally efficient and robust strategy for humanitarian medical logistics in resource-constrained, post-disaster settings.

title: Podium Placement in LLM Enhanced Entrepreneurial Contests: Theory and Evidence
affiliations: Villanova University, Villanova University - School of Business and

detail.title: Podium Placement in LLM Enhanced Entrepreneurial Contests: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: We examine how entrepreneurs optimize their search strategies when using Large Language Models (LLMs) for technology commercialization. The fundamental tension arises from using standardized AI tools to create competitively differentiated value, especially when a contest selects a broad set of performers on a podium, rather than a single winner. We take a two-step approach to this problem. We first build a formal model to characterize podium placement in terms of four variables: contest seeds, friction in using LLMs, workarounds, and product definition capability, when contestants follow either breadth first (B) or depth first (D) search strategies while using LLM. The model separates expected performance from podium-placement probability and shows how contest selectivity influences the efficacy of search strategies. In the second step, we run a randomized control trial to reveal a sharp distinction between process inputs and podium placement. The empirical findings qualify the model-based predictions. When every contestant uses the same LLM, friction, number of ideas, level of LLM usage, and workaround levels are statistically indistinguishable across treatments and performance quartiles. What predicts top-quartile placement is competitive awareness-the ability to recognize what differentiation the contest demands-exceeding the predictive power of product sophistication, elaboration, or prompting behavior. Search strategy shapes not just how many ideas a contestant generates, but whether the contestant perceives the competitive pressure the contest is applying.

title: The Impact of Social Climate Changes on Identity Disclosure and Inclusion in the Workplace
affiliations: Queen's University - Smith School of Business

detail.title: The Impact of Social Climate Changes on Identity Disclosure and Inclusion in the Workplace
detail.abstract: Employees with concealable stigmatized identities (e.g., LGBTQ+ status, neurodivergence, invisible disabilities) choose how much to disclose at work, and firms decide how strongly to invest in inclusion programs. Both decisions are influenced by an anticipated shift in the external social climate, which neither party controls. I develop a two-period principal-agent model of this relationship. Identity disclosure cannot be fully retracted, as it persists in the organization's memory. I show that the firm may strategically provide high inclusion early on to incentivize disclosure, and then cut inclusion supports later. This allows the firm to extract surplus from the employee who is locked in by what is already known about her. Exploitation of this disclosure persistence can be optimal for the firm even in stable or improving social climates, when one would not expect disclosure irreversibility to matter. I also show that more organizational memory is not always worse for employees: the organization's memory can serve as an implicit commitment device, although the employee's preferred level of memory is always weakly below that of the firm.

title: Thinking Against the Wind: Narratives, Information, and Reasoning Ability
affiliations: Shandong University - Center for Economic Research,  and Shandong University

detail.title: Thinking Against the Wind: Narratives, Information, and Reasoning Ability
detail.abstract: This study examines how reasoning ability is associated with individuals' responses to authoritative narratives and related information. We conducted a two-wave survey experiment at two pivotal moments in the pandemic, comparing distinct populations exposed to contrasting narratives. In the first wave, the dominant narrative emphasized the virus's severity and strict lockdowns; by the second wave, it shifted toward downplaying health risks and advocating for lifting lockdowns. Both waves included a randomized information intervention presenting statistics on COVID-related mortality. We find that individuals with higher reasoning ability consistently tend to "think against the wind," challenging prevailing narratives regardless of their direction. The information intervention significantly shifted the beliefs of high reasoning ability individuals when evidence contradicted the dominant narratives but had little effect when it aligned with them. Furthermore, high reasoning ability individuals were more skeptical of competing non-authoritative narratives. Overall, these patterns highlight the important association between reasoning ability and changes in public opinion and policy support, particularly in belief updating under conflicting narratives.

title: Exposing Healthcare-Sector Misconduct Through Activist Short Selling: Evidence from Pharmaceutical, Biotechnology, and Medical Device Companies

detail.abstract: This review tries to answer three main questions about activist short selling in the healthcare industry. The first question is whether short selling keeps patients safe from companies that are doing harmful things. The second question is about which other investors have tried similar strategies and how their methods compare to one another. The third question is how short selling stacks up against other ways of making powerful companies answer for their actions. To explore these questions, the review takes a close look at the work of Fahmi Quadir, who began her career as a forensic analyst and later became a well-known activist short seller in the healthcare space. The review mainly uses her 2018 ProMarket interview to understand how she thinks about her work and the methods she uses. It also looks at real short selling campaigns that were carried out against companies like Valeant Pharmaceuticals, St. Jude Medical, and Mallinckrodt to see what the outcomes were. The review pulls from academic studies, legal documents, and official regulatory filings to support its conclusions. The review finds that activist short selling is the fastest tool out there for exposing fraud inside corporations and that it uniquely rewards the people who can uncover it. However, the benefit to patients tends to be indirect because it can take down a harmful business model without fixing the damage that has already been done to people. The strategy also has some serious built-in weaknesses. Short sellers pick their targets based on how much money they can make rather than how badly patients are being hurt. The rules around short selling are also becoming stricter as time goes on. Most of these campaigns barely turn a profit once all the borrowing costs and legal fees are considered. Because of all this, short selling is best thought of as one important piece of a bigger system for holding companies accountable rather than a complete solution on its own.

title: The Hidden Cost of Failed Payments: SEC Disclosure of Payment Losses, Chargebacks, Write-offs, and Unrecovered Funds, 2020-2025

detail.title: The Hidden Cost of Failed Payments: SEC Disclosure of Payment Losses, Chargebacks, Write-offs, and Unrecovered Funds, 2020-2025
detail.abstract: This study analyzes annual SEC filings from 50 public payments, fintech, marketplace, cross-border payments, B2B payments, and related financial technology companies from fiscal years 2020 through 2025. The purpose is to measure how often public companies quantify payment-loss exposure in securities filings, how much they disclose when they do, and whether a consistent disclosure framework exists for this category of operational risk. The central finding is a disclosure gap: no standardized SEC reporting category exists for payment-operational losses, and companies that do quantify this exposure use at least 50 different accounting labels to describe what is operationally a related family of risks, including chargebacks, transaction losses, unrecovered funds, settlement exposures, and payment-related write-offs. Of 285 prepared company-years analyzed, only 44 (fewer than 1 in 6) contained a validated quantified disclosure, and 83.3% of those disclosures appeared in financial statement footnotes rather than in narrative risk sections. The market does not receive a consistent, comparable signal about payment-loss exposure from public-company filings. The supporting quantitative finding is that the 16 companies that did disclose quantified amounts reported a combined $3.45 billion in validated payment-loss exposure from 2020 through 2025, drawn from a narrow subset of the 50-company universe. Of that amount, $2.67 billion was classified as realized losses, write-offs, or unrecovered funds, while $790.9 million was classified as reserves or provisions. The $2.67 billion realized-loss subtotal is the most conservative headline figure because it excludes reserve and provision rows that may reflect expected losses or period-end balances rather than completed economic losses. These totals represent a conservative lower bound on disclosed exposure, not an estimate of total industry losses. Four companies (Block, Uber, Airbnb, and Robinhood) accounted for approximately 87.0% of the raw validated dollar amount. The SEC's 2023 cybersecurity disclosure rules established a precedent for standardized reporting of operational risk categories. No equivalent standard applies to paymentoperational losses, despite the growing scale of global payment infrastructure and the demonstrated inconsistency of existing disclosures. Extraction was performed on financial statement footnotes, MD&A, risk factors, and controls sections using an LLM-based analysis pipeline. Of 174 deduplicated candidate findings, 78 were included in the final dataset and 96 were excluded. One additional finding was identified through post-extraction manual review and added to the dataset, bringing the total to 79 included findings across 45 company-years. The 2025 fiscal year data is incomplete due to filing availability at the time of analysis and should not be interpreted as evidence of declining exposure. The full validated dataset and excluded-findings audit file are available for independent review.

title: When the Selic Reaches the Factory Floor: A High-Dimensional DSGE-Benchmarked Canonical Monetary Transmission Framework for Brazil
affiliations: University of Minho

detail.title: When the Selic Reaches the Factory Floor: A High-Dimensional DSGE-Benchmarked Canonical Monetary Transmission Framework for Brazil
detail.abstract: CMTF-Brazil measures how Selic tightening travels from COPOM decisions to Brazilian industry. It extracts monetary and productive-sector states with RCCA, estimates compact SVAR responses, separates CHANGE and HOLD meetings through Rigobon-Sack heteroskedasticity, maps sectoral pain with local projections, and benchmarks aggregate timing against SAMBA. detail.abstract: This study examines the favorite-longshot bias in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) prediction markets on the Kalshi platform. Analyzing 95 contracts across 12 months with 58,138 price observations, we find no evidence of the classic favorite-longshot bias. Contracts priced at zero exhibited perfect calibration, winning 0% of the time. When excluding zero-price contracts, lowprobability contracts (prices between 0.01 and 0.28) showed slight overpricing with a bias of-0.08 (p < 0.001), while high-probability contracts (prices above 0.70) were well-calibrated with a bias of-0.03 (p = 0.589). The overall market outperformed random guessing by 26.6% (Brier Score = 0.1835). These findings suggest that CPI prediction markets are efficient at the extremes and do not exhibit the favorite-longshot bias commonly found in sports betting markets. We discuss implications for market design and the interpretation of prediction market prices as information aggregation mechanisms.

detail.title: A Theory of Bank Liquidity Requirements
detail.abstract: We develop a general equilibrium theory of financial intermediation and its implications for liquidity regulation. The model is built around an agency problem arising from leveraged intermediation: banks finance loan origination with deposits and face moral hazard in risk management, while holding cash mitigates these incentives at the cost of foregone investment returns. Liquidity demand therefore emerges endogenously from incentive considerations rather than from exposure to exogenous funding shocks. In equilibrium, financial experts choose between allocating equity to the banking sector relative to the non-bank financial sector that can provide ex-post liquidity by buying bank assets. Asset prices are determined endogenously in liquidation states, linking banks’ ex ante liquidity choices to market liquidity and the allocation of intermediation across sectors. Comparing the decentralized equilibrium to a planner’s allocation, we show that liquidity regulation mandating higher cash holdings improves incentives within banks but is not sufficient to implement the efficient allocation. In particular, it leads to an inefficiently large banking sector that free-rides on liquidity provision by non-bank investors. Implementing the planner’s allocation requires a second policy instrument, such as limits on bank size or subsidies to equity-financed liquidity provision outside the banking sector.

detail.abstract: The Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights fundamentally altered international pharmaceutical patent law by imposing uniform minimum standards across all World Trade Organization Member States. While the TRIPS Agreement and the 2001 Doha Declaration formally preserve significant public-health flexibilities, including compulsory licensing, parallel importation, and the sovereign right to set rigorous patentability standards, the proliferation of TRIPS-Plus bilateral and regional free trade agreements has rendered those flexibilities progressively ineffective in practice. Through mechanisms of data exclusivity, patent linkage, and investor-State dispute settlement, developed economies have constructed a regulatory architecture that seals the very safety valves which developing countries fought to preserve at Doha. This article examines the legal contours of multilateral health flexibilities under the TRIPS framework, analyses the manner in which bilateral instruments erode those flexibilities, and evaluates, through comparative case studies of India, South Africa, and Brazil, how sovereign States have sought to protect pharmaceutical access in a hostile trade-law environment. The article further addresses the paradigm shift occasioned by the biologics revolution and the COVID-19 pandemic, which exposed the structural inadequacy of patent-centric flexibilities when operative monopolies are sustained by trade secrets governing proprietary manufacturing know-how. The article advances the thesis that the prevailing international intellectual property regime is systemically incapable of delivering equitable pharmaceutical access to the Global South without structural reform at the multilateral and domestic levels, and proposes a concrete agenda for that reform encompassing automatic pandemic waivers, binding technology-transfer obligations, investor-State dispute settlement reform, and alternative research-and-development financing mechanisms.

detail.abstract: This paper makes one claim exact. Procedural fairness cannot reduce the waste of positional competition, only recompose it, and conformity selects the wasteful equilibrium even where a better one exists. In a screening contest with any degree-p homogeneous effort cost, contestants burn exactly 1/p of the rent at every fairness weight, by Euler's theorem. Conformity, derived from one monitoring-and-sanctioning primitive under random cross-sector matching, makes occupational flow bistable, and the average payoff advantage over opponent shares decides which equilibrium is played. Imitation and patience select by that scalar, the global game brackets it, and the uniform average is the unique aggregation that never disagrees with risk dominance. Pure hysteresis point-identifies the selection rule in panels, the panel-restricted set is sharp, and inference survives estimated boundaries. Korean mean margins are null while the regulated long-hours tail breaks on statutory schedule and rebounds when enforcement wavers, the joint pattern the theory predicts.

detail.title: Does the Novel Market Sentiment Measure Work? A Preregistered Out-of-Sample Replication
detail.abstract:
This study presents a preregistered out-of-sample replication of the market-forecasting result reported in Holmberg (2024), where a variable derived from the Global Consciousness Project (GCP) appeared to improve stock-market forecasting models. Two frozen specifications were compared under a preregistered design (OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/JK24C): Model A, a benchmark using conventional market and volatility variables, and Model B, which adds lagged Max[Z] values and related interaction terms. The preregistered hypothesis was that Model B would outperform Model A in total return, directional hit rate, and Sharpe ratio. The evaluation covers 198 trading days from late June 2025 until March 31, 2026, when a disruption of the original GCP data stream ended the prospective simulation earlier than planned. An exploratory continuation using GCP 2.0 data is reported separately.

In the base specification, which excludes the structurally unusual U.S. government shutdown period, Model B outperformed Model A on all three preregistered metrics. Total return increased by 7.60 percentage points, the Sharpe ratio rose by 0.07, and the directional hit rate improved marginally from 65.25% to 65.96%. Including the shutdown period, Model B retained a smaller return advantage of 3.06 percentage points and a higher Sharpe ratio, although its directional hit rate fell below that of the benchmark. The exploratory GCP 2.0 continuation showed a similar return-channel pattern only when the constructed proxy preserved directional block structure, suggesting a clearer target for future preregistered tests using successor-network data.

The results reproduce the central pattern of Holmberg (2024), where the one-year public out-of-sample simulation found relative return gains of 5.1–13.9 percentage points, while directional gains were at most 2.5 percentage points. Across two prospective windows spanning roughly 450 trading days and covering different market environments, the GCP-dependent specification has therefore outperformed its benchmark in return terms in both evaluations, while the directional-accuracy advantage remains more fragile and context dependent.

In summary, the combined evidence suggests that the incremental contribution of the GCP-derived terms does not primarily appear through better day-by-day directional classification. Instead, it appears mainly in the size and timing of the trades on which the two models disagree, which is reflected in higher simulated returns and risk-adjusted performance. As such, the results support a narrower, twice-observed pattern: GCP-derived attention-related variables may contain incremental forecasting information under particular market conditions.

detail.title: Is Expected Market Volatility a Priced Risk Factor?
detail.abstract: We study which sources of risk in expected market volatility are priced by investors. We construct a portfolio of index options spanning short-term forward variance, whose return identifies shocks to expected volatility while remaining immune to price jump risk. Its average return is negative and significant. We decompose this return into three orthogonal components: dynamic market and market-neutral cross-sectional stock positions hedging variance and a stock-unrelated residual. Most of the premium comes from the dynamic market component and the residual. Thus, once dynamic market exposure is accounted for, expected market volatility is not a separate cross-sectional risk factor.

detail.title: When Disagreement Cuts Both Ways: Pricing Cash-Flow Disagreement in Stocks and Bonds
detail.abstract: Analyst earnings forecast dispersion, a standard proxy for investor disagreement, negatively predicts stock returns. We show that the same measure positively predicts corporate bond returns. We propose a unified explanation based on disagreement about issuers' cash flows: because equity is a convex claim on firm cash flows whereas debt is a concave claim, cash-flow disagreement raises the average valuation of equity but lowers that of debt, generating opposite return predictability across securities issued by the same firm. Consistent with this mechanism, the negative relation between disagreement and stock returns concentrates among firms with more option-like payoffs, while the positive relation between disagreement and bond returns concentrates among bonds close to default. Our study shows that the asset pricing implications of disagreement depends critically on payoff structure, rather than having a uniform sign across asset classes.

detail.title: Endogenous Nature of the Economic Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the medium-term Juglar business cycle is an intrinsic property of an operationally closed economic system rather than a response to external shocks. The oscillation is treated as an emergent property of a network of economic actions rather than an aggregate of individual agents: this distinguishes the approach from agent-based modeling and brings it close to the rule-based evolutionary ontology of micro-meso-macro. It is shown that, through positive and negative feedback, the recursive organization of economic processes necessarily generates endogenous oscillations typical of complex nonlinear systems. During a crisis the structural disproportions that accumulated in the upswing are eliminated. The paper examines the competitive self-regulation mechanism in its pure form, as a necessary precondition for understanding how the economy functions under real-world conditions of monopolization, financialization, and so on. The cycle is shown to move along a trajectory between two turning points-"producers are unwilling to produce more" and "consumers are unwilling to consume less." The gradual upswing and the sharp crash are explained structurally: breaking an economic link requires only one party's decision, whereas restoring it demands coordination among all parties. A forward model is presented that reproduces this dynamics without any external driver, and two crisis circuits are identified-commodity and financial. The paper concludes that anti-crisis policy based on supporting aggregate demand is ineffective: the crisis is merely postponed, while structural distortions persist, accumulate, and eventually lead to a deeper crisis.

detail.title: The Latent Nature of Sexual Corruption as an Obstacle to the Realisation of the Constitutional Right to Effective Legal Protection
detail.abstract: The article examines the latent nature of sexual corruption as a significant obstacle to the realisation of the constitutional right to effective legal protection. It is argued that sexual corruption should not be understood as an isolated instance of individual deviance, but as a specific form of abuse of power, influence, or control over access to a significant benefit, whereby a person’s dependence is covertly transformed into a condition of sexualised subordination. Particular attention is paid to the problem of apparent voluntariness, since the victim’s outwardly consensual conduct may be incorrectly interpreted as participation in an unlawful exchange. The article substantiates the claim that such “voluntariness” may in fact result from structural dependence, fear of losing an important opportunity, the threat of an adverse decision, reputational risks, or the absence of real mechanisms for safe refusal and complaint. It is emphasised that the criminalisation of sexual corruption must be compatible with constitutional values, including the rule of law, justice, and the priority of human rights. Accordingly, a victim should not be treated as a culpable participant in a sexual-corruption exchange where the interaction primarily involved his or her own exploitation and did not entail the sexual exploitation of third parties. The article concludes that an effective criminal-law model for countering sexual corruption must not only identify the corrupt use of power for sexualised purposes, but also guarantee real protection for the victim, including safe reporting mechanisms, protection against retaliation, and safeguards against victim-blaming and reputational harm.

title: The New Frontier of Intellectual Property Disputes: Arbitration, Arbitrability and the Evolution of Intellectual Property Dispute Resolution

detail.title: The New Frontier of Intellectual Property Disputes: Arbitration, Arbitrability and the Evolution of Intellectual Property Dispute Resolution
detail.abstract: The increasing importance of intellectual property (IP) rights in a technology-driven global economy has led to a corresponding rise in complex and high-value IP disputes. These disputes range from traditional copyright, patent, trademark, and licensing disputes to emerging issues such as Fair, Reasonable and Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) disputes involving Standard Essential Patents (SEPs). While litigation before national courts remains a common method of dispute resolution, arbitration has emerged as an attractive alternative, especially in cross-border and multi-jurisdictional disputes. Arbitration offers several advantages, including confidentiality, neutrality, expert determination, procedural flexibility, and the international enforceability of arbitral awards. However, the effectiveness of arbitration as a mechanism for resolving IP disputes depends largely on the arbitrability of the rights and claims in question. This paper examines the role of arbitration in the resolution of IP-related disputes and analyzes the concept of arbitrability as a key determinant of the validity and enforceability of arbitral awards. It considers the various categories of IP disputes, the circumstances in which questions of arbitrability arise, and the approaches adopted in selected jurisdictions, including Nigeria, Hong Kong, Singapore, China, England, and Australia. The paper finds that there is growing international acceptance of arbitration as a mechanism for resolving commercial intellectual property disputes, including complex licensing and FRAND disputes involving standard-essential patents. However, significant divergence remains in relation to disputes concerning the validity and subsistence of registered intellectual property rights, which continue to raise public policy concerns in many jurisdictions. The paper concludes that notwithstanding these differences, arbitration is increasingly positioned as a central mechanism for the resolution of cross-border intellectual property disputes, particularly in light of the globalization of innovation, technology transfer and SEP licensing.

detail.abstract: ESP32 Marauder is a portable firmware environment for ESP32-class microcontroller boards that exposes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth security-testing functions through a screen interface, serial command-line interface, and, in some deployments, a Flipper Zero companion workflow. This paper examines ESP32 Marauder as a low-cost wireless research platform rather than as a general-purpose penetration-testing substitute. The analysis separates the platform into two operational models: standalone ESP32 Marauder devices and ESP32 Marauder devices controlled through Flipper Zero. Particular attention is given to the common confusion around “5G Wi-Fi.” In wireless LAN research, this term should be interpreted as 5 GHz Wi-Fi, not cellular 5G. Most classical ESP32, ESP32-S2, and ESP32-S3 Marauder boards are limited to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi because of radio hardware constraints. Current Marauder releases, however, explicitly identify ESP32-C5 support for 5 GHz operation, and Espressif documents ESP32-C5 as a dual-band 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi 6 system-on-chip. The central argument is that Marauder’s capability boundary is determined primarily by the radio chipset, board wiring, firmware target, storage arrangement, antenna design, and regulatory environment—not by the name “Marauder” itself. The paper concludes with controlled laboratory usage documentation for wireless surveying, frame observation, beacon demonstration, handshake education, rogue access point awareness, Bluetooth Low Energy observation, and wardriving. Active disruption and credential-capture functions are treated only as controlled research topics under authorization, with explicit ethical boundaries.

title: Territorial Capital Allocation Index: A Multidimensional Framework for Infrastructure Investment Prioritization

detail.title: Territorial Capital Allocation Index: A Multidimensional Framework for Infrastructure Investment Prioritization
detail.abstract: The allocation of infrastructure capital across competing territorial claims is one of the leastresolved problems in applied investment analysis. Existing competitiveness indices-including the EU Regional Competitiveness Index and derivatives of the World Economic Forum's Global Competitiveness Index-are built primarily to inform policy rankings rather than investment decisions. They measure territorial potential in aggregate but offer limited guidance on where capital is most likely to generate returns, where fiscal capacity constrains co-investment ability, or how institutional barriers translate into project-level risk. This paper proposes the Territorial Capital Allocation Index (TCAI), a multidimensional composite framework designed explicitly for infrastructure investors and development finance institutions operating across heterogeneous regional environments. The TCAI integrates four core pillars-institutional quality, infrastructure absorption capacity, fiscal and financial readiness, and human capital and market depthweighted through an investor-oriented methodology that reflects actual capital deployment constraints. We apply the framework to a comparative scenario analysis involving regions at different stages of institutional and economic development, demonstrating how the TCAI produces investment prioritization signals that diverge meaningfully from rankings generated by conventional competitiveness measures. The paper also derives a set of practical recommendations for international development banks, sovereign wealth funds, and private infrastructure investors seeking to operationalize territorial analysis in capital allocation decisions.

title: U.S. Policies Unintentionally Accelerated China's Open AI Ecosystems
affiliations: , University of Chicago - Department of Economics, Marshall School of Business - University of Southern California, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and University of Chicago - Department of Sociology

detail.title: U.S. Policies Unintentionally Accelerated China's Open AI Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Over the past decade, U.S. policies have increasingly aimed to preserve artificial intelligence (AI) leadership by promoting domestic free-market policies while controlling global technological chokepoints, particularly advanced semiconductors and computational infrastructure. These measures raised the cost of Chinese AI development, but they also increased the strategic value of open and locally adaptable AI systems. Before raising export controls on high-performance chips, both the U.S. and China promoted policies that included support for opensource AI. During the period following major U.S. export-control shocks, China increasingly embedded open-source AI into national technology strategy through proposed ecosystem building, standards coordination, and resilience-oriented deployment. Moreover, Chinese developers increased engagement with open-source large language model repositories substantially more than U.S. developers did, consistent with a shift toward open infrastructure under geopolitical constraints. Subsequently, Chinese-origin open models diffused widely through open-source communities and scientific research. Even though such models remained largely absent from U.S. patent disclosures, American commercial entities use them in open-access research, suggesting their undermeasured importance within the foundation of U.S. commercial activity. These findings suggest that technological containment policies may unintentionally accelerate open innovation ecosystems as a competitive response, with implications for global leadership in both academic and commercial artificial intelligence.

title: On Normative Power and Exploitative Abuse in Digital Markets – Navigating Heike Schweitzer's Notion of the Private Law Society
affiliations: Ilmenau University of Technology

detail.title: On Normative Power and Exploitative Abuse in Digital Markets – Navigating Heike Schweitzer's Notion of the Private Law Society
detail.abstract: Normative power has been defined as ‘the power to shape current and future normality, normativity, markets, social relations, behaviour, and truth‘. In digital markets, this power stems not only from the formal power to set the rules of engagement, but also from the more subtle ‘steering’ and design capabilities that dominant platform operators and ecosystem orchestrators enjoy. This gives them a unique ability to exclude competitors and exploit users at scale. This paper aims to better understand the nature of this power and scrutinize competition law’s ability to tackle its exclusionary and exploitative effects. To this end, the paper draws inspiration from two concepts put forward by Heike Schweitzer: rule-setting (regulatory) power as market power; and her notion of the norms that shape the private law society as a decentralized coordinating system. Expanding the former notion of rule-setting power to encompass novel manifestations of normative power, the paper uses insights from the latter to ascertain when and how competition law intervention into exploitative practices is possible.

detail.abstract: This article examines the Lead Independent Director (LID) as a documentarily observable mechanism of independent leadership within the Board of Directors. Corporate governance literature and practice often use the proportion of independent directors as an indicator of the quality of board oversight. Although relevant, this criterion may lead to an excessively formalistic interpretation, since the nominal presence of independent directors does not, by itself, ensure effective coordination, influence over the agenda, qualified access to information, oversight of management, treatment of conflicts of interest, or engagement with shareholders. Based on a critical review of the literature and a comparative documentary benchmark, this study classifies independent leadership arrangements in Brazilian and international companies, using the cases as illustrative and comparative documentary evidence, without claiming statistical generalization, causal inference, or measurement of behavioral effectiveness. The article contributes by proposing a conceptual distinction between formal independence and substantive independence, a documentary coding protocol, an operationalization matrix for substantive independence, an exploratory application of the Documentary Substantive Independence Index to the main cases, and an exploratory documentary diagnostic matrix for independent board leadership.

affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and National University of Singapore (NUS) - NUS Business School

detail.title: U.S. Tax Reform and International Trade
detail.abstract: We examine how changes in the taxation of multinational income affect U.S. firms' crossborder trade in physical goods. We study this question in the context of the 2017 U.S. tax reform, which substantially changed the tax treatment of multinational income. To examine whether these changes translated into real trade responses, we use firm-level shipping container data that capture physical goods exports and imports. Using a quasi-difference-indifferences approach, we find that after the tax reform, U.S. firms that are more exposed to the reform's international tax provisions significantly increase their physical goods exports and imports relative to less-exposed firms. The effects are stronger for firms with higher pre-tax profitability, greater R&D intensity, and lower shipping costs, consistent with a tax-based explanation. Furthermore, we document an increase in intersegment sales across geographic segments. Our study provides the first empirical evidence on the tax reform's effect on U.S. firms' cross-border trade in physical goods.

title: Discounted Deterrence: How a Cut in the Price of a Violation Reshaped Workplace-Safety Enforcement

detail.title: Discounted Deterrence: How a Cut in the Price of a Violation Reshaped Workplace-Safety Enforcement
detail.abstract: In July 2025 the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration raised the penalty discount for establishments with 11 to 25 employees from 60 to 70 percent, a roughly 25 percent cut in the expected penalty, and left every other size band unchanged. Using the full federal enforcement record, this paper estimates the effect on the violations the agency cited. Cited violations per programmed inspection at the treated band fell by about a fifth to a third, with precise zeros at every unmoved band, and the decline survived placebo policy dates, a nevertreated state-plan comparison, a targeting check, and a citation-timing battery. Early injury data show no corresponding safety improvement. Because a price cut moves both a firm's compliance incentive and the enforcer's own citing behavior in the same direction, the enforcement record cannot by itself reveal which changed, and independent harm data are required to adjudicate. The findings caution against reading enforcement counts as compliance when a sanction price has moved.

detail.abstract: Modern financial and managerial decision systems increasingly reward the integration of heterogeneous data, but integration is not costless. It introduces delay, engineering effort, coordination burden, model complexity and the risk that a decision-relevant signal becomes stale before it is acted upon. This working paper proposes the Entropy-Certainty Matrix, a decision-timing framework for assessing when an organisation should wait for fuller information integration and when it may rationally act on an early high-certainty signal. The framework separates two constructs that are often conflated: market entropy, defined as the unpredictability, fragmentation and informational disorder of the decision environment; and metric certainty, defined as the reliability, timeliness, actionability and known error structure of a particular signal. It further specifies the unit of analysis, construct boundaries, causal mechanisms and scope conditions under which the framework is expected to apply. The paper develops a normalised integration-premium score that compares the cost of waiting with the incremental accuracy value expected from further integration. It positions the framework relative to established entropy-finance literature, value-of-information analysis, speed-accuracy trade-offs and decision-latency research. An illustrative Monte Carlo simulation using synthetic decision episodes shows how fast-path and integrated-path strategies can be compared across entropy-certainty conditions. The simulation is not offered as empirical validation; rather, it demonstrates how the framework generates falsifiable predictions and guides future backtesting or field evidence. The core claim is that waiting is valuable only when the expected accuracy gain from integration exceeds the time, operational, coordination and staleness costs imposed by delay.

title: Functional Inversion and Exit: A Theory of Human-Centered Adaptive Systems
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Functional Inversion and Exit: A Theory of Human-Centered Adaptive Systems
detail.abstract: Human-centered systems depend upon representations in order to coordinate action across individuals, organizations, and institutions. Yet the conditions that motivate participation are not directly observable within these representational systems. This paper develops a theoretical framework describing how adaptive relationships are maintained across multiple layers of translation connecting psychological experience, individual behavior, social coordination, and institutional organization. The proposed Human Translation Architecture consists of five functional layers: Psyche, Centers of Gravity, Personality, Social Coordination, and Institutions. Within this framework, Centers of Gravity represent relatively stable organizations of psychological tension that guide adaptation across time, while Personality functions as a translation system that generates strategies for addressing those tensions within reality. The paper introduces Significance as an evaluative signal generated by the Psyche regarding the degree of correspondence between outcomes and active Centers of Gravity. Building upon this architecture, the paper develops the concept of Functional Inversion, a process through which higher representational layers increasingly optimize their own representations rather than the conditions they were originally created to serve. Institutional drift, manipulation, and alienation are interpreted as consequences of this process. The paper further argues that meaningful exit mechanisms function as corrective channels through which lower-layer evaluations can influence higher-layer structures when correspondence deteriorates. The framework contributes a general model of hierarchical adaptation failure and proposes Functional Inversion as a unifying mechanism linking psychological, organizational, and institutional forms of self-referential adaptation.

detail.abstract:
What Virginia Is Spending, What Virginia Is Getting (v5.0) is the comprehensive statewide reference on data center development in Virginia and the anchor volume for a series of county case studies. It carries forward the fiscal and ratepayer analysis of version 4.0 (March 2026) and adds three new components: a complete operating-and-pipeline inventory of 286 Virginia data center facility records across at least 24 counties and cities; the full record of enacted and proposed state policy; and a regional synthesis that maps the county portfolio onto the commonwealth.

The report finds that Virginia's data center sales and use tax exemption (Code of Virginia 58.1-609.3(18)) cost the commonwealth $1,941,390,000 in forgone state revenue in FY2025, that the available but-for evidence, from JLARC's December 2024 study, a University of Georgia econometric model, and the broader incentives literature, consistently indicates a substantial share of Virginia's data center investment would occur without the exemption, and that data center load growth exposes residential ratepayers to infrastructure costs that Dominion Energy's own filings project will roughly double monthly bills within a decade. Data centers already consume about 25 percent of Virginia's electricity.

Version 5.0 also assembles the complete state policy record: the exemption statute and its history, the jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction equipment-tax rate landscape, the data center bills enacted in the 2026 General Assembly session, the State Corporation Commission's new GS-5 large-load rate class, the Dominion integrated resource planning dockets, and the FY2027 budget impasse in which the exemption is the central dispute. Appendices include the full facility inventory, a register of canceled and rejected projects, the key-operator list, the state study library, and the companion county volumes.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Tax Governance: A Comparative Survey
affiliations: Texas A&M University (TAMU), School of Law and Texas A&M University School of Law

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Tax Governance: A Comparative Survey
detail.abstract: Tax administrations worldwide are deploying artificial intelligence (AI) to detect fraud, select audits, and process returns, generating efficiency gains alongside new risks to privacy, fairness, and due process. This article compares how seven jurisdictions (the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, India, China, and Japan) govern the use of AI in tax administration. Drawing on primary legislation, case law, regulator guidance, and official reports current to mid-2026, it maps each jurisdiction's data-protection baseline, AI-specific instruments, taxpayer rights to contest automated decisions, and oversight and redress mechanisms. Across very different legal traditions a common imperative emerges: AI may augment but not replace human judgment, and taxpayers retain rights to explanation, human review, and challenge. The jurisdictions diverge in method. The EU and Brazil are rights-based and enforceable, the United States and India principles-based and remedial, China centrally supervised, and Japan soft-law and consensual. The United Kingdom occupies a middle ground, relaxing formal rules while preserving transparency and recourse. Situating these approaches against the United Nations Tax Committee's 2025-2029 work programme on global best practices for AI in tax, the article argues that durable tax principles, namely legality, ability to pay, and taxpayer rights, should anchor AI governance as the technology advances.

title: The Dichotomous Coverage Model: When Formal Networks and Informal Paratransit Collide in a Megacity
affiliations: , Lagos State University, Ojo-Lagos, Nigeria and Lagos State University, Ojo-Lagos, Nigeria

detail.title: The Dichotomous Coverage Model: When Formal Networks and Informal Paratransit Collide in a Megacity
detail.abstract: Across Global South megacities, bus reforms seek to transform informal paratransit into formal networks. However, even successful formal services on major corridors coexist with thriving informal sectors in unreached spaces. This paper introduces the Dichotomous Coverage Model to explain this phenomenon, drawing on Metropolitan Lagos, where a century of reform has produced a bifurcated mobility landscape. Integrating spatial interaction theory, institutional analysis, and empirical evidence from the Lagos Bus Reform Initiative, including a commuter survey (n=1,023) and operational data from 120 formal routes, the model argues that formal networks and informal paratransit occupy distinct niches: spatial legibility versus operational penetration; scheduled reliability versus spontaneous responsiveness; infrastructural formality versus institutional embeddedness; network hierarchy versus capillary reach. Illustrative evidence from fourteen global cities suggests recurring spatial typologies of formal-informal coexistence. The paper concludes that the complete formalisation may be unattainable; sustainable mobility requires strategic integration that leverages the complementary strengths of both systems.

title: Governing the Demand Shock: Local Institutional Variation in Virginia's Data Center Expansion
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Governing the Demand Shock: Local Institutional Variation in Virginia's Data Center Expansion
detail.abstract: Governing the Demand Shock reads Virginia's data center buildout as a single demand shock absorbed by twelve local governments under sharply different institutional conditions, and asks why their outcomes diverged. Drawing on the full corpus of Virginia county and regional case studies, it builds a five-posture framework for how localities meet large-load industrial demand: reform-after-entitling, refusal-before-entitling, contract-lock, governance-capture, and pre-entitlement-by-ordinance. The decisive variable is timing, whether a jurisdiction reforms its land-use and fiscal tools before or after the industry arrives, and the central finding is that local leverage is a depreciating asset that contracts as entitlements accumulate. Contract-lock arrangements, such as Chesterfield's thirty-year $0.24 rate and Botetourt's twenty-year cap, are the one effectively irreversible move; Mecklenburg, with fifteen years of operating data centers, is the lone case in which outcomes can be audited rather than projected. The analysis is built entirely from public records and is written to remain useful regardless of how individual projects resolve.

title: The Maverick Model: Distribution-Weighted Demand and Capital Accumulation

detail.title: The Maverick Model: Distribution-Weighted Demand and Capital Accumulation
detail.abstract: This paper develops the Maverick Model, a demand-centered model of capital accumulation in which income distribution affects productive capacity through heterogeneous household consumption behavior and demand-driven investment. Households are grouped by income shares and group-specific marginal propensities to consume. These differences imply that aggregate consumption depends not only on total income, but also on the distribution of income across households with different spending propensities. The model shows how this distribution-weighted consumption channel enters expected demand, how expected demand determines investment, and how investment changes the future capital stock. The baseline result is that a higher distribution-weighted propensity to consume raises steady-state capital and output under a concave investment specification and a standard local stability condition. The paper also distinguishes this baseline distribution-capacity result from a stronger stagnation result. A globally concave investment response does not by itself generate low-capacity traps. Such traps require an additional threshold or nonconvex investment response to expected demand. The model therefore establishes two related but distinct claims. First, income distribution can affect long-run productive capacity through demand-driven capital accumulation. Second, demand-driven stagnation can arise when investment requires expected sales to exceed a viability threshold. The analysis clarifies why high saving, low interest rates, or rising financial wealth need not produce strong real investment when expected demand is weak. It also generates empirical implications for consumption, investment, capital formation, and state-dependent fiscal effects.

title: Time Preferences under Stress
affiliations: , The University of Sydney, The University of Sydney and The University of Sydney - School of Economics

detail.title: Time Preferences under Stress
detail.abstract: We test whether acute psychosocial stress affects time preferences in a laboratory experiment. Using a validated stress induction and an incentive-compatible elicitation of time preferences, we find no statistically detectable effect of acute stress on patience or present bias, despite strong physiological and self-reported stress responses. These results suggest that, in our laboratory setting and within the precision afforded by our sample, acute psychosocial stress does not appear to systematically alter intertemporal decision-making. They also highlight the need to examine whether chronic or domain-specific stressors have more robust effects.

title: Suptech-Powered Consumer And Investor Protection Supervision. Architectural Pathway From Reactive Oversight To Outcome-Driven Institutional Intelligence.
affiliations: and

detail.title: Suptech-Powered Consumer And Investor Protection Supervision. Architectural Pathway From Reactive Oversight To Outcome-Driven Institutional Intelligence.

declarations.funderStatement: Gates Foundation

detail.abstract:
Consumer and investor protection supervision (CIPS) is undergoing a structural transition. While financial authorities have made substantial progress digitizing complaint handling, case management, and supervisory workflows, the analytical capabilities required to transform these data assets into anticipatory, outcome-driven supervision remain unevenly developed. This report argues that the principal constraint is no longer the availability of technology, but the absence of integrated supervisory data architectures capable of converting fragmented signals into actionable intelligence. Authorities frequently deploy individual components—portals, databases, dashboards, chatbots, and analytics tools—without the architectural integration required to create a coherent supervisory pipeline.  

Drawing on four years of State of SupTech survey data, a longitudinal dataset covering hundreds of financial authorities, and the GovSpace corpus of 102 documented CIPS suptech implementations across 73 countries, the report develops the concept of the “foundation-to-intelligence transition.” It shows that adoption has concentrated in complaint and conduct signal capture, while more advanced capabilities—including early warning systems, predictive analytics, algorithmic auditing, vulnerable-consumer profiling, and other anticipatory functions—remain limited or absent in most jurisdictions. The challenge is no longer moving from no data to data, but from signals to intelligence.  

To address this gap, the report applies two complementary frameworks: the GovTech Generations 3.0 maturity model and the DataStack Blueprint. Together, they provide a diagnostic and design methodology for assessing supervisory capability across data collection, processing, storage, analytics, data products, interoperability, and governance, while identifying the sequencing required to advance from reactive oversight toward AI-augmented and agentic supervision.  

The report concludes with a practical decision framework that links architectural development to six outcome categories—Access, Deterrence, Welfare, Coverage, Speed, and Intelligence Quality—and offers a structured pathway for financial authorities seeking to build supervisory systems that not only process information, but measurably improve consumer and investor outcomes.

title: Source-of-Gain Auditing for Supervised Multimodal Fusion: A Controlled ECG-CXR-Structured-Variable Benchmark for Retrospective Cardiovascular-Code Status
affiliations: Lancaster University and Lancaster University

detail.title: Source-of-Gain Auditing for Supervised Multimodal Fusion: A Controlled ECG-CXR-Structured-Variable Benchmark for Retrospective Cardiovascular-Code Status
detail.abstract: Multimodal fusion benchmarks often credit gains to architecture without auditing how much is recoverable from non-modality variables, availability, or structured covariates. We introduce the Source-of-Gain Audit (SoGA) and its Source-of-Gain Decomposition, a reporting protocol and estimator that attribute a measured supervised multimodal gain to named sources (non-modality floor, modality content, availability, fusion-head capacity, label shortcuts) before any is credited to architecture. We instantiate it on a controlled ECG-CXR-structured-variable benchmark for retrospective ICD-coded cardiovascular-status classification: 54,357 MIMIC-IV patients with ECG and seven pre-ECG structured variables, 33,223 with a matched chest radiograph (CXR), under fixed patient-level splits, labels, and evaluation. In the single-lead testbed, a non-modality floor using no waveform or image reaches AUC 0.826, close to the trimodal 0.859. The decomposition assigns modest per-source residuals over ECG: under a competent 12-lead reference, structured variables contribute +0.019 and CXR +0.015 (single-lead gives the looser upper bounds +0.032 and +0.027). Under a narrower major-cardiac label the residual over the floor grows to +0.056, preserving the trimodal > bimodal > ECG ordering. Within this audit, no complex fusion head significantly exceeds concatenation among the fifteen heads (practical equivalence within +/-0.01 AUC), so the residual is attributable to modality content and structured covariates. The broad code-based label admits residual leakage (bounded at <=0.012 AUC), so the benchmark serves methodological evaluation, with clinical deployment beyond its scope. Supervised multimodal gains should clear these non-modality and shortcut controls before being credited to fusion architecture.

title: Progressive information purification for multi-modal cancer survival prediction
affiliations: Anhui Medical University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Anhui University

detail.title: Progressive information purification for multi-modal cancer survival prediction
detail.abstract: Cancer survival prediction based on pathology and genomics is important for assessing prognosis and planning treatment. Pathological images reflect spatial phenotypes such as tumor morphology and the tumor microenvironment, but they are also affected by ice-crystal artifacts and scanner noise. Genomic data describe the overall molecular status of a patient, while multiple molecular signals are often encoded into the same representation, making key prognostic information difficult to distinguish. Therefore, directly aligning or fusing pathology and genomics may introduce noise and prevent useful information from both modalities from being fully used. To address these issues, we propose Progressive Information Purification Network (PIP-Net), a framework for pathology-genomics multi-modal survival prediction that performs information purification across multiple stages. First, to evaluate the contribution of different pathological patches to prognosis, we design Drop Probability Prediction in the Pathology Purification stage to perform preliminary screening on each patch and subsequently conduct information purification under the constraint of the proposed Drop Loss. Second, to avoid mixing different types of pathological information, Information Separation separately aggregates modality-shared and pathology-specific information through two branches, allowing them to participate in prognostic modeling in different ways. Finally, to reduce redundant information in genomic representations, Genomic Purification refines genomic features and combines them with modality-shared and pathology-specific representations to obtain the final patient-level representation. Experiments on five public TCGA datasets demonstrate that PIP-Net achieves the highest average C-index of 69.38%, outperforming the second-best method by 1.62%. The code will be released upon acceptance of the paper.

title: The Price of Exclusion: SME Set-Asides in Public Procurement

detail.title: The Price of Exclusion: SME Set-Asides in Public Procurement
detail.abstract: Set-asides expand small-firm access to public procurement by removing rival bidders from the auction. When the excluded bidders are the ones forming the price, the policy replaces competition with eligibility at a high static cost. I study São Paulo's centralized electronic procurement platform, where a legal reinterpretation expanded SME-only tendering into medical and hospital supplies. The platform's reverse auctions record losing bidders' drop-out prices, which reveal willingness to supply; I use them to split the setaside price effect into the competitive discipline lost when non-SMEs are excluded and the offset from the post-policy SME pool. In standardized non-pharmaceutical markets the protected pool responds but does not replace the lost discipline: the full set-aside generates a static welfare loss of 28.9 percent of the open-regime price at λ = 0.30. Pharmaceutical procurement shows larger but more model-sensitive losses. A 10 percent SME price preference keeps non-SMEs in the auction at near-zero price cost while delivering less redistribution. The relevant frontier is not SME support versus none; it runs between exclusionary redistribution and support that preserves the price-forming pool.

title: India's Demographic Dividend to 2050
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: India's Demographic Dividend to 2050

detail.abstract: India's demographic dividend is often presented as a growth advantage created by a large working-age population. This paper argues that the stronger policy question is not whether India is young, but whether the country can convert its age structure into productive employment, rising incomes, and fiscal resilience before aging pressures rise. Using a desk-based synthesis of demographic projections, labor-force data, health and fertility evidence, and selected academic literature, the paper develops a conversion framework with six filters: health, learning, labormarket entry, job quality, productivity and inclusion. It finds that India's dividend remains real but uneven, conditional, and time-bound. The main constraints are labor absorption, female employment quality, weak school-to-work pathways, state-level divergence, and delayed aging preparation. The paper contributes a transparent scenario framework, reproducible figure data, an implementation constraint analysis, and a monitoring dashboard for tracking demographic conversion to 2050.

title: Household Debt Overhang and Bankruptcy abuse Prevention
affiliations: School of Finance, Nankai University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Central University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Household Debt Overhang and Bankruptcy abuse Prevention
detail.abstract: Bankruptcy abuse prevention has been criticized for increasing foreclosure rates, imposing negative impacts on housing markets, and aggravating the financial crisis. By contrast, this paper documents that bankruptcy abuse prevention reduces household debt overhang, a phenomenon harmful to home values and housing markets. Using a difference-indifferences analysis, we find that households in recourse states increased their home improvement and maintenance expenditures after the Bankruptcy Abuse Prevention and Consumer Protection Act, a period during which the households paid considerable attention to the downside risk of the housing market, and that the effects vary by home equity level. The results remain unchanged with alternative specifications and cannot be explained by credit changes, judicial and nonjudicial foreclosures, homestead exemption, house sales, or heterogeneous expectations. Last but not least, we use entropy balancing to eliminate the differences between the treatment and control groups and get similar results.

title: The Impact of Soft Law on Social Change: Measurable Objectives for Achieving Gender Diversity on Boards of Directors
affiliations: University of Technology Sydney (UTS), University of Technology, Sydney and

detail.title: The Impact of Soft Law on Social Change: Measurable Objectives for Achieving Gender Diversity on Boards of Directors
detail.abstract: In 2010 the Australian Securities Exchange's Principles of Corporate Governance were amended to include three new recommendations dealing with gender diversity in listed corporations. The recommendations suggest that companies implement a diversity policy, set measurable objectives for achieving gender diversity and measure the number of women at various levels of the organisation. This article examines companies' early response to the amendments. It presents an empirical analysis of the disclosures made by ASX 200 companies in their 2011 annual reports. The article builds on and develops research carried out by the authors for the 2012 Australian Census of Women in Leadership which found that, although the number of women on corporate boards had increased since 2010, there was not a similar increase in women in senior executive teams. It presents evidence that there are positive changes being implemented in the majority of ASX 200 companies that should, over time, make a difference to the ability of women to reach positions of leadership. The Australian approach of encouraging change through organisation-wide policy improvements and targets will hopefully improve female representation along the length of the pipeline to leadership and not only at the top. The ASX policy was formulated in the context of an international debate regarding the relative benefits of quotas and targets in achieving gender diversity on boards. In major European countries mandatory quotas were adopted, while in Australia and other countries voluntary targets set. Quotas secure substantial change through compliance, while targets may encourage change through strategic initiatives. This research examines early evidence of the impact of both hard and soft law on social change.

title: A Riemann Wald Couple
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Riemann Wald Couple
detail.abstract: We give a probabilistic reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) in which the non-trivial zeros appear twice: as the characteristic zeros of Pólya's symmetric law X ξ (characteristic function Ξ(t)/Ξ(0)), and as the exponential rates of its van Dantzig/Wald dual H ξ. The dual is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC); on the critical line it is the explicit infinite convolution H ξ = γρ>0 Exp(rate γ 2 ρ), U 1/2 = γρ>0 δ γ 2 ρ , the Thorin measure being the counting measure on the squared ordinates. Two analytic ingredients organise the construction. Polson's Gamma(2) scale mixture makes the primal kernel infinitely divisible (Kristiansen), and the 2 sin 2 lemma-which makes-log ζ(σ + it)/ζ(σ) negative-definite for σ > 1 via the kernel 2 sin 2 (tx/2) against the von Mangoldt measureexhibits the relevant positivity unconditionally for σ > 1. These act on the primal side; the dual's Lévy density κ satisfies U = L-1 [κ], and the dual is a GGC-equivalently κ completely monotone, equivalently the signed measure U Polson recovers by Stieltjes inversion is positiveif and only if RH. We are careful to note that this dual condition admits no weaker unconditional floor: on the dual side, infinite divisibility, GGC and RH coincide, and the primal ID floor does not reduce it. Riemann's incomplete-gamma representation, an everywhere-convergent form, carries the construction into the strip 1 2 < σ < 1. A numerical audit confirms the governing identity to five significant figures over λ ∈ (0, 100) and resolves U into peaks at γ 2 ρ. We keep a two-tier discipline throughout-construction unconditional, positivity of U RH-equivalent. The reformulation is an equivalence, not a proof.

title: Better Disclosure, Higher Rates: Algorithm Aversion and the Cost of Debt
affiliations: Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics (ZUFE) and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Better Disclosure, Higher Rates: Algorithm Aversion and the Cost of Debt
detail.abstract: Firms increasingly use large language models to draft their annual reports. We measure the share of AI-generated narrative in the annual reports of Chinese A-share firms from 2009 to 2025 using the ZeroGPT detector and ask how it affects the cost of debt. A one-standard-deviation rise in AI-generated content increases the effective interest rate on debt by about 0.23 percentage points and lowers the bank-loan-to-assets ratio by roughly one percent of its mean. The penalty is not explained by weaker disclosure. AIassisted reports are more readable, repeat less prior-year boilerplate, and are no more likely to be restated; they also improve the equity information environment, raising analyst coverage and cutting forecast errors. Creditors charge more anyway. We read this as algorithm aversion: machine-written text carries a detectable signature, and lenders-who must extend trust and bear the downside-distrust disclosure that reads as written by a machine rather than a person, independent of its content.

title: The Citizens Standard: A Macroeconomic Model of a Two-Circuit Monetary System
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Citizens Standard: A Macroeconomic Model of a Two-Circuit Monetary System
detail.abstract: This paper develops a macroeconomic model of the Citizens Standard, the constitutional monetary architecture set out in the preceding papers of this series. The model decomposes the money stock by use — a transactional circuit that prices goods and an asset circuit that holds claims on the productive economy — and derives the framework’s macroeconomic behavior from that single structural device. Three results follow. First, K1/K2 issuance lands in the asset circuit as a portfolio-choice equilibrium rather than by assumption: a wealth-neutral forced sale has a zero direct propensity to consume, so newly created money raises asset values held by citizens rather than consumer prices, with a bounded second-order leak that shrinks as the universal equity floors mature (Proposition 1). Second, although the framework makes the issuing authority a large, price-insensitive purchaser of equity, forward returns settle at a bounded valuation premium rather than collapsing — the purchaser is a net buyer while the floors accumulate and a bounded net seller as they mature, with a deceased citizen’s residual passing to an heir’s floor rather than being sold — and firm-side equity supply responds to valuation (Proposition 2). Third, the architecture’s distributional instrument — a direct, equal citizen dividend — is also its fastest stabilization instrument: under price-level-path targeting it operates as an automatic countercyclical stabilizer that reaches households without depending on the credit channel, while the slow ownership channels are correctly relieved of stabilization duty. The model is explicitly short-run non-neutral and makes contact with the standard New Keynesian framework rather than departing from it; it differs in the locus of money creation and the ownership of newly issued claims, not in the rigidity assumptions. A recurring structural feature is that the framework’s strained window is its youth: the price-level leak, the householdsaving channel, and the return-compression premium are all largest at launch and resolve over a single maturation horizon. Beyond these results the model adds a consumer-dividend channel (K3) that pays a growth-indexed, equal citizen dividend out of the same real-growth budget that funds the floors — bounded by the price-stability locus rather than stacked on top of it — and that, by diverting issuance away from index purchases, also caps the Proposition 2 premium directly. The model’s load-bearing simplification — a partition of money by use — is an approximation rather than an institutional wall, and the paper is explicit about where that partition is porous and what is required to calibrate the three quantities the results leave open.

title: The Citizens Standard: Banking, Inside Money, and the Two-Circuit System
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Citizens Standard: Banking, Inside Money, and the Two-Circuit System
detail.abstract: This paper extends the macroeconomic model of the Citizens Standard (Neo-Solon, 2026e) to a commercial banking sector. The architecture issues outside money into two circuits — a transactional circuit that prices goods and an asset circuit that holds citizen equity — but in any modern economy banks create inside money, deposits, when they lend, raising a natural worry that inside-money creation could undermine the price-stability, controllability, and circuit-separation results established for outside money alone. Layering a reduced-form banking block on the two-circuit model yields five results. First, the price level is set by total transactional money — outside money plus the transactional share of deposits — so the inflation-gap throttle must target the total and offsets deposit creation one-for-one, and the model's forward-looking determinacy carries over to the augmented aggregate. Second, inside-money creation is bounded by capital, reserve, and collateral constraints; because the citizenship floors are locked and therefore non-pledgeable, the collateral constraint binds and holds the inside-money transactional share near one-eighth, against more than a third were citizen wealth fully pledgeable. Third and fourth, the throttle retains control of the price path so long as inside deposits stay below a buffer-adjusted threshold, and that threshold maps directly into a minimum capital — or reserve, or loan-to-value — requirement, yielding a macroprudential design rule that ties Basel-style stringency to monetary controllability. Fifth, because locked floors cannot be withdrawn, the bulk of citizen wealth is run-proof: systemic run severity and the lender-of-last-resort burden scale only with the small liquid share. A single structural feature — the lock — unifies the results. The banking block is explicitly reduced-form; a microfounded balance-sheet treatment and the allocative efficiency of intermediation are left to future work.

title: Beyond the Tipping Point: A Retrospective SEWI Analysis of AIR9000 Phase 2, 4 and 6 (MRH90 Taipan Helicopters) â€" The Termination Case

detail.title: Beyond the Tipping Point: A Retrospective SEWI Analysis of AIR9000 Phase 2, 4 and 6 (MRH90 Taipan Helicopters) â€" The Termination Case
